purpose: Governed reusable problem-solving strategies learned from successful Adaptive executions. Validated strategies may guide planning; runtime candidates remain advisory until repeated or promoted.

strategies.title: Resolve ambiguity with an analysis-only Work Unit before speculative implementation
guidance: Stop retrying implementation when the same unresolved blocker remains.
Create one read-only DECISION or RESEARCH Work Unit focused only on resolving blockers.
Reconcile canonical requirements, use cases, architecture, handoff and existing implementation before proposing anything new.
Classify each blocker as: existing project decision, technical decision not yet materialized, genuine business-rule ambiguity, or environment/tooling limitation.
Apply existing decisions directly; choose the smallest safe technical option when it does not change business behavior; ask the human only for genuine business decisions.
Produce an explicit decision matrix and implementation contract, then resume code in a separate bounded Work Unit.
safety: Do not invent business rules to unblock implementation.
Do not modify implementation files during the blocker-resolution Work Unit unless explicitly authorized.
Preserve checkpoints before resuming risky implementation.
evidence: 2026-09-12: a repeatedly blocked backend restoration task became implementable after an analysis-only Work Unit reconciled canonical documents, classified blockers, consolidated the technical contract and confirmed that no new business decision was required.

strategies.title: Reduce planning scope after malformed structured planner output
guidance: Do not repeat the same broad planning request unchanged.
Retry once with a smaller objective and exactly one bounded Work Unit.
Prefer a read-only reconciliation or blocker-resolution Work Unit when uncertainty is the cause.
Validate the structured plan before any repository mutation.
If the simplified retry also fails, stop safely and preserve the last checkpoint instead of bypassing the orchestrator.
safety: Never fall back to ungoverned direct execution when project policy requires the bridge.
Do not treat malformed planner output as authorization to relax schema validation.
evidence: 2026-09-12: repeated ProjectPlanningError/invalid JSON failures stopped after replanning was reduced to one small Work Unit and the unresolved blocker was isolated first.

strategies.title: Trace result integrity across transport boundaries before retrying the work
guidance: Do not assume that a terminal-looking field or conversation history is the authoritative machine result.
Trace the same execution across producer, transport, persistence, and consumer boundaries before changing the task or model.
At each boundary compare stable identity, byte/character length, completion markers, and SHA-256 when available.
Treat progress output and terminal summaries as presentation channels unless integrity is explicitly proven.
If corruption or truncation occurs after the worker produced a complete result, fix result transport instead of retrying the original work.
safety: Do not reconstruct a missing machine result from a truncated presentation channel.
Do not relax parser/schema validation to make corrupted transport appear valid.
Do not increase a human-facing progress limit as a substitute for an authoritative result channel.
evidence: 2026-09-13: a planner JSON failure was traced from complete model output to OpenClaw progress formatting, where an 8000-character presentation limit appended ...(truncated)...; terminalReply was later proven to be a short visible summary rather than the original payload.

strategies.title: Keep execution control messages small and move large agent results through durable artifacts
guidance: Use the agent runtime for dispatch, liveness, progress, cancellation, and short terminal summaries.
Publish authoritative worker output to a durable result store before declaring completion.
Pass stable result references between dependent Work Units instead of copying large payloads into prompts or chat messages.
Use manifest-last publication with execution identity, completeness, byte length, and SHA-256 so consumers can verify integrity before use.
Keep project-owned runtime results inside the governed project boundary rather than mixing them with orchestrator-owned global state.
safety: Do not treat chat history as a durable inter-agent message bus.
Do not commit runtime result artifacts to the project repository.
Do not allow result paths to escape the governed project result root.
evidence: 2026-09-13: Adaptive adopted <project>/.adaptive/runs/<orchestration>/<work-unit>/<execution>/ with result.txt, summary.md, and manifest.json, then changed dependency fan-in to pass manifest references instead of large inline results.

strategies.title: Preserve run identity and reconcile observation timeouts before redispatching work
guidance: Persist run identity immediately after dispatch and before the first wait.
Distinguish a wait/observation timeout from execution failure; a timed-out wait may leave the run active.
Reconcile the same run within a bounded global budget before creating another execution.
Do not redispatch solely because result retrieval or observation failed.
Record the ordering of run state, terminal receipt, result persistence, and result availability when diagnosing lifecycle races.
safety: Bound reconciliation attempts and preserve the circuit breaker.
Use explicit abort/cancel operations only when cancellation is intended.
Never create duplicate side-effecting work until the previous run state is known.
evidence: 2026-09-13: OpenClaw agent.wait was verified to use per-call wait windows; timeout does not itself cancel the run, cancellation is separate, and the client already treats intermediate wait timeout as RUNNING.

strategies.title: Use staged SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE payload tests with stop gates to isolate transport defects
guidance: Start with a small deterministic payload, then a medium payload near the suspected boundary, then a large payload beyond it.
Embed unique BEGIN and END markers and record length/hash so completeness can be proven independently of semantic content.
Stop escalation when MEDIUM fails; diagnose that boundary before running LARGE.
Use the real production transport path for the final proof, not only deterministic unit mocks.
Keep the project under test read-only until the transport channel itself has passed.
safety: Do not use production project mutations to diagnose a transport layer.
Do not declare robustness from unit tests alone when the real runtime contract has not been exercised.
evidence: 2026-09-13: SMALL succeeded through agent.wait, MEDIUM exposed that terminalReply was only a 237-character summary for a 5266-character source payload, and LARGE was intentionally withheld until the transport architecture was corrected.

strategies.title: Preserve authenticated execution identity across observer processes
guidance: Sign the exact effective connect facts: challenge nonce and timestamp, sent credential, ordered scopes, client mode, platform and device family.
Use least-privilege Gateway scopes and persist only sanitized execution identity before the first wait.
Recover the same run and governed Result Store target before considering redispatch; never call agent again merely because the observer process ended.
Fail closed when recovery records are invalid or point outside the current project Result Store.
safety: Never persist credentials, private keys, prompts or worker results in run identity records.
Treat observation-channel failure as distinct from execution failure.
evidence: 2026-09-13: a new Python process recovered the same runId, execution_id and ResultStoreTarget and retrieved an authoritative adaptive-result-store result without a second agent dispatch.

strategies.title: Prove the effective child runtime before repairing an apparently missing dependency
guidance: Do not immediately reinstall a dependency when the configured environment already contains it.
Preserve the original traceback and identify the exact failing process before changing the environment.
Prove repository, branch, HEAD, configured interpreter, effective interpreter, sys.prefix, sys.base_prefix, sys.path and the relevant Python environment across the process boundary.
Reproduce the import through the exact launcher, executable and environment used by the failing runtime.
Inspect interpreter path canonicalization and symlink handling; preserve the authorized virtualenv interpreter path instead of collapsing it into a system interpreter path.
Do not install the package globally merely to hide an environment, launcher or provenance defect.
After the runtime contract is understood, add a fail-closed prerequisite preflight that uses the same executable and environment as the real launch.
safety: Do not print credentials, tokens or the complete inherited environment during provenance diagnostics.
Do not use global dependency installation as a workaround for a project virtualenv defect.
Do not reset, clean or destroy unrelated working-tree state while diagnosing runtime provenance.
If the historical failure cannot be reproduced exactly, distinguish confirmed evidence from the suspected mechanism instead of inventing certainty.
evidence: 2026-09-15: the Adaptive Bridge reported jsonschema missing even though jsonschema 4.26.0 was installed in the authorized venv. Forensics proved the failure occurred in the first Bridge child before Planner/provider execution; stale interpreter-path canonicalization was removed, the logical venv path was preserved, and a deterministic fail-closed runtime prerequisite preflight was added and verified through the real OpenClaw path.

strategies.title: Use an explicit plan-only path instead of overloading executor limits
guidance: Do not overload an execution-limit parameter with a different semantic meaning merely to suppress execution.
Keep valid executor invariants unchanged when introducing a diagnostic or planning-only path.
Use an explicit plan-only mode that executes the real RuntimeProjectPlanner and all structured-output validation but stops before the generated project Work Unit executor.
Prove separately that the Planner runtime executed and that generated project Work Units were not dispatched.
Return a machine-readable ProjectExecutionPlan so planning can be inspected, tested and audited without project mutation.
safety: Plan-only must not be reported as successful project execution.
Do not emit worker-completion evidence for Work Units that were only planned.
Do not weaken Planner JSON Schema or semantic validation for diagnostic convenience.
Do not use max_waves=0 or another invalid executor value as a hidden plan-only switch.
evidence: 2026-09-15: a Planner smoke attempted max_waves=0 to prevent Work Unit dispatch, but the executor contract correctly required 1..256. Adaptive added explicit --plan-only mode; the real Planner then produced a schema-valid, semantically valid ProjectExecutionPlan with three Work Units while dispatching zero generated Work Units.

strategies.title: Classify tracked WIP, staged changes, untracked generated files, and stash separately before blocking a safe fast-forward
guidance: Do not equate a literally non-empty working tree with tracked WIP that makes an update unsafe.
Classify repository state into four independent categories before deciding: tracked unstaged modifications, staged modifications, untracked files, and historical stash entries.
Use git diff --name-only and git diff --cached --name-only to prove whether tracked/staged WIP exists; use git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all to inspect untracked files separately.
A historical stash can remain untouched while the current checkout is updated; its mere existence is not a reason to block a fast-forward.
Generated untracked caches such as __pycache__/ and *.pyc do not by themselves block a safe fast-forward when they do not collide with files the update needs to write.
If tracked and staged diffs are empty and the only untracked paths are disposable/generated caches, preserve those files physically and perform only a fast-forward update such as git pull --ff-only.
After the update, verify HEAD, git status, and git stash list so preservation is proven rather than assumed.
If Git reports that an untracked file would be overwritten, or if any tracked/staged modification exists, stop and preserve state for an explicit decision instead of cleaning or overwriting.
safety: Never use git reset --hard, git clean, stash pop/apply/drop, or ad-hoc rm -rf merely to make a repository appear clean enough for an update.
Never create a new stash automatically when preservation policy forbids changing existing WIP state unless explicitly authorized.
Do not discard generated untracked files merely because they are not important; preservation and safe update can coexist.
Prefer git pull --ff-only so repository synchronization cannot silently create a merge commit.
Treat any path-collision warning from Git as a stop condition rather than deleting the untracked file.
evidence: 2026-09-16: during SGFP Stage 11, an ariel-agent-skills Bridge update was incorrectly blocked because __pycache__/ directories and a preexisting stash made the checkout look non-clean. The reusable correction is to classify tracked, staged, untracked, and stash state separately: only tracked/staged WIP or an actual untracked-path collision prevents a preservation-safe fast-forward; generated caches and historical stash entries may remain untouched.

strategies.title: Use correlated persisted execution evidence when conversational memory disagrees
guidance: When chat/session memory says work is active but persisted operational evidence disagrees, reconcile the persisted execution state before waiting or redispatching.
Treat Result Store/checkpoint identity, active execution records, valid leases and fresh heartbeats as stronger evidence than conversational narrative.
If no correlated live execution exists, do not tell the user or scheduler to keep waiting merely because an earlier message said the worker was running.
Preserve the old attempt as history and let the orchestrator choose governed recovery from the current persisted state.
safety: A checkpoint alone is history, not proof of current liveness.
Do not kill or redispatch a worker until correlated execution identity and liveness have been reconciled.
evidence: 2026-09-18: during SGFP Stage 11 recovery, OpenClaw conversational state described revision work as active while Control Room/Result Store showed the Work Units blocked and active_executions empty. Recovery became correct only after persisted state was treated as authoritative.

strategies.title: Require worker identity plus lease/heartbeat correlation before treating a process as useful active work
guidance: Do not treat an operating-system PID, launcher process, dashboard RUNNING label, or controller heartbeat by itself as proof that a useful worker is active.
Correlate orchestration_id, work_unit_id, execution_id/external_id, worker identity, lease and fresh heartbeat before suppressing recovery.
Distinguish controller/launcher liveness, worker liveness and Work Unit progress as separate facts.
If the launcher survives but no correlated worker/lease/heartbeat exists, classify the state as stale/suspect and return it to governed recovery.
safety: Do not infer absence of work from one missing telemetry source when other correlated liveness evidence is fresh.
Do not create a duplicate side-effecting worker while a valid correlated lease/heartbeat still exists.
evidence: 2026-09-18: recovery audit found a successor launcher PID alive without identifiable worker descendants or sufficient worker lease/checkpoint evidence. The process alone was not enough to prove useful execution.

strategies.title: Do not let historical observability debt indefinitely block a technically validated artifact
guidance: Evaluate product/artifact readiness from its own technical evidence: accepted corrections, tests, lint/static gates, Result Store integrity and absence of conflicting/corrupting changes.
Track orchestration observability gaps as a separate infrastructure incident when they do not invalidate the artifact evidence.
Stop recursive recovery-of-recovery when the remaining uncertainty is only historical orchestration observability rather than a functional or integrity defect in the artifact.
Report both dimensions explicitly, for example READY_FOR_ENVIRONMENTAL_RETEST plus ADAPTIVE_OBSERVABILITY_DEBT.
safety: Do not waive a real functional, security, integrity or concurrency conflict by relabeling it observability debt.
Require explicit evidence that the artifact itself is intact before decoupling the infrastructure incident.
evidence: 2026-09-18: SGFP corrections and Result Stores were technically sound, but repeated recovery/audit units were blocked by insufficient historical lease evidence. Separating Adaptive observability debt allowed the SGFP state to be correctly declared READY_FOR_ENVIRONMENTAL_RETEST.

strategies.title: Use a controlled A/B component isolation and native logs before speculative repair
guidance: Reproduce the failure on the smallest stable entry point before changing code.
When safe, compare behavior with the suspected component enabled versus disabled while holding the environment constant.
If the failure disappears only when that component is removed, inspect the platform-native logs immediately after reproduction for the exact causal stack.
Repair the smallest contract violation proven by the log and repeat the same A/B/environmental test.
safety: Do not disable unrelated security controls permanently as a diagnostic shortcut.
Do not claim causality from correlation alone when the A/B result is ambiguous or other variables changed.
evidence: 2026-09-18: gestaopessoal.org /wp-login.php failed only while SGFP was active. Disabling SGFP restored login; WordPress PHP logs then identified WordPressLogin::safeRedirect receiving WP_Error where the callback accepted only WP_User. The minimal contract fix restored the login path.
